memos.headline: A routine deal step: shareholders of First Hawaiian and TriCo approved the agreed merger
reasoning: Source: the companies' joint release on GlobeNewswire (dated 10/29), relayed by Benzinga 09:02 ET: 'their respective stockholders and shareholders have approved the proposed acquisition of TriCo by First Hawaiian ... expect the transaction to close later in 2026'.
What changed: an expected vote passed. Pre-market on the consolidated tape: 53.40 vs 53.455, -0.1%.
objections: Expected shareholder vote on an announced deal.

memos.headline: The buyer's side of a routine step: Viatris's sub starts the agreed $36.50 tender for Pacira
reasoning: Source: Viatris's release, relayed by Benzinga Newsdesk 08:43 ET: 'Viatris Subsidiary Peach Purchaser Sub Commences Tender Offer To Acquire Pacira Biosciences For $36.50/Shr'. The deal was agreed earlier; this starts the mechanics.
For Viatris (a $22B company), the deal was priced when announced. Nothing new today.
objections: Routine step; the buyer's exposure was priced at announcement.

memos.headline: VTRS: no trade. Tender launch on an agreed deal
reasoning: Filter gap: tender-offer launches by a named subsidiary ('Sub Commences Tender Offer') now count as routine without needing 'previously announced' in the text. A hostile bid would not come from a purchaser sub set up for an agreed deal.

memos.headline: A cut to consensus: iRadimed trimmed its EPS range to $2.07-$2.11, where analysts already were ($2.11)
reasoning: Source: iRadimed's Q3 release, via Benzinga Newsdesk 08:33 ET: 'Lowers FY2026 Adj EPS Guidance from $2.09-$2.24 to $2.07-$2.11 vs $2.11 Est; Narrows FY2026 Sales Guidance from $91.000M-$96.000M to $91.600M-$93.100M vs $92.133M Est'.

What changed: the guidance range narrows down onto consensus. The EPS midpoint ($2.09) is 1% below the estimate and the sales midpoint ($92.35M) is about at it. Analysts were already at the low end. Pre-market: no trades on the consolidated tape.
objections: A narrowing to consensus; little new.
